content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates in the middle to late horizon when prices are trending upward — likely due to lagging response to new data.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects downward — model reacts too quickly to volatility.
- Mean reversion behavior is overemphasized — model too aggressively pulls prices back toward historical averages, ignoring recent momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 10-day forecasts are more accurate than 30-day; 30-day forecasts suffer from cumulative lag and smoothing errors.
- When true outcome shows strong upward trend, model lags and underestimates — should adjust upward with increasing confidence in momentum.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections in model forecasts unless recent history shows clear downward pressure — often misses early signs of decline.
